title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: JUNE'S THANKSGIVING
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about June, a hotel night manager from Albuquerque, New Mexico.
June can calm a lobby full of angry guests at three in the morning.
But this year, her mom handed her something scarier. Thanksgiving.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE HANDOFF
segments.quote: In preparing for battle I have always found that plans are useless, but planning is indispensable.
segments.author: Dwight D. Eisenhower
lines: Twenty-two relatives. One small kitchen. And June had never cooked a turkey.
Her old boss, an Army man, kept a line from General Eisenhower above the desk:
In preparing for battle I have always found that plans are useless, but planning is indispensable.
So June stopped panicking and planned. Who brings what. What cooks when.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE PERFECT TABLE
segments.quote: Have no fear of perfection - you'll never reach it.
segments.author: Salvador Dali
lines: But the plan kept growing. Cloth napkins. Three pies. Name cards in gold ink.
Her friend Tina laughed, and held up her coffee mug, with a line from the painter Salvador Dali:
Have no fear of perfection - you'll never reach it.
June crossed out two pies and the gold ink. The rolls would come from a bag.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE FROZEN BIRD
segments.author: John Heywood
lines: Thanksgiving morning, the turkey was still a block of ice. She had read the box wrong.
I once tried a hair dryer on mine. Don't ask.
June wanted to fix it alone. Then her mom called with an old English saying:
Many hands make light work.
So June gave everyone a job. Her dad's job was staying out of the way.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE GRAVY WAR
segments.quote: Laughter is the sun that drives winter from the human face.
segments.author: Victor Hugo
lines: By four, Uncle Ray and her brother were fighting about gravy.
Then her dad tripped over the dog, and the gravy landed on Uncle Ray.
June almost cried. Then she remembered Victor Hugo, the French writer:
Laughter is the sun that drives winter from the human face.
So June laughed first. Then everyone did. Even Uncle Ray. The gravy war was over.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE APOLOGY
segments.quote: Usually, one's cooking is better than one thinks it is.
segments.author: Julia Child
lines: Dinner was two hours late, and the turkey was a little dry. June stood up to say sorry.
Then she saw her mom's old cookbook, with a line from the chef Julia Child written inside:
Usually, one's cooking is better than one thinks it is.
So June sat down, said nothing, and watched Uncle Ray go back for thirds.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE TOAST
segments.quote: Gratitude is not only the greatest of virtues, but the parent of all the others.
segments.author: Cicero
lines: At the end of the night, her mom asked June for a toast. She thought of Cicero, the Roman speaker:
Gratitude is not only the greatest of virtues, but the parent of all the others.
So she thanked every person at that table, one by one. Even the dog.
Her mom smiled. Same time next year. Your house.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Plan ahead. Skip perfect. Ask for help. Laugh first. Stop apologizing. Say thank you.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Make a plan. Forget perfect. Ask for help. Laugh first. Stop apologizing. And say thank you, out loud.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And please, read the turkey box.
